subject: Post-demo: DPA sequencing, residency & log retention clarifications
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Thorpe <emily.thorpe@medisync.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: follow-ups on DPA sequencing, residency & logging

Thanks again for the demo this morning — really helpful to see the two pilot workflows. Quick recap and a small list of clarifying asks so our legal/ops teams can prep a tailored DPA redline.

Open items we took away from the call:
- Data roles: you mentioned Medisync would be controller for patient notes and Redwood would act as processor for model inference. Can you confirm that mapping (controller = Medisync, processor = Redwood) for the pilot scope?
- Residency requirement: you flagged a US-only hosting requirement for PHI-derived outputs during the pilot. Is that strict (US-only) or would US + EU (restricted regions) be acceptable?
- Logging & retention: what is the minimum audit log retention window you need for security/compliance? You said "long enough for audits" — looking for a target in days (e.g., 90/365/730).
- Subprocessor notifications & breach sequencing: what notification SLA do you need from Redwood for subprocessor events (initial triage vs formal notice)?

What we need from you by EOD Friday to keep timelines: confirmation on controller/processor mapping and residency requirement. If you can also share any contract redline priorities (PII handling, deletion windows, notification windows), that will help prioritize legal review.

Next steps from our side: I'll loop in legal for a redline and Priyom will draft a short technical note describing our residency controls and the sample log export schema. Attaching a one-page tech summary will follow in a separate email.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198

--
Attachment placeholders: redlined_DPA_v2.pdf (stub), log_schema_sample.csv (stub)
From: Benji Peterson <benji.peterson@medisync.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Thorpe <emily.thorpe@medisync.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jul 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: follow-ups on DPA sequencing, residency & logging

Thanks Hannah — great summary. A few answers/clarifications from our side:

- Controller/Processor: yes, Medisync will be controller for patient-provided content and clinical notes. Redwood is expected to be processor for inference and transient derived outputs, though we will want explicit language about not using customer data for model training.
- Residency: for the pilot we require US-only (data centers physically located within the contiguous US). If Redwood can provide a formal commitment for the pilot window, we can consider expanding later.
- Logs/retention: for HIPAA audits we typically want 365 days of immutable audit logs, but for the pilot our compliance lead said 180 days would be acceptable if we can export logs on demand.
- Subprocessor/breach timeline: initial technical alert within 48 hours (signaling triage started) and formal written notice with impact assessment within 7 calendar days. We may have to shorten the formal notice window depending on findings.

Two asks for Redwood ops/engineering: can you provide a sample log export (CSV with fields and timestamps) and confirm whether Redwood supports region-bounded model hosting (i.e., dedicated inference pool restricted to us-west region)?

If you can attach a draft DPA redline we can mark high-priority clauses for legal. Happy to hop on a 30-min ops call next week.

Best,
Benji
Benji Peterson
Director, Platform Security | Medisync Health
benji.peterson@medisync.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jul 2028 18:10:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: suggested answers & materials for Medisync follow-ups

Looping you both with suggested technical wording we can send to Medisync. Copying quick notes for legal and infra.

Suggested replies (technical):
- Controller/processor: we will accept processor role for inference as long as the scope is limited to model hosting/inference and we are excluded from any obligations that would require audit of our internal model training processes. Add explicit clause: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to improve, train, or fine-tune its models without Customer's prior written consent."
- Residency: we can enforce region-bound hosting at the tenant level. For the pilot we can lock the deployment to our us-west public cloud region (data & KV caches within US-only). Formal commitment window: pilot term only; ask legal for permanent residency language.
- Log retention & export: we support configurable retention tiers (90 / 180 / 365 / 730 days). We can provide on-demand exports (CSV) and a streaming syslog integration. For HIPAA audits recommend 365 days immutable retention; for pilot offer 180 days with export capability.
- Subprocessor notification: propose initial triage alert within 48 hours and a formal incident summary within 72 hours (we usually take up to 7 days for final impact analysis). Legal may want 72h/7d split; we should be flexible.

Attachments to prepare now:
- log_schema_sample.csv (sample fields + timestamps)
- redlined_DPA_v2.pdf (initial legal redline)

Notes for legal (Laura): can you confirm acceptable wording for "no-training" clause and whether we should accept a 48h initial alert / 7d formal notice or push for 72h formal notice as our default? Also need to confirm whether residency commitment needs a separate SLA.

I'll draft the outbound message once you confirm.

--
Priyom Das
Staff Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Thorpe <emily.thorpe@medisync.com>, Benji Peterson <benji.peterson@medisync.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: follow-ups on DPA sequencing, residency & logging

Hi Emily & Benji — thanks for the quick replies and for prioritizing the residency constraint. Attached are two artifacts we discussed: 1) a redline with our initial legal position (redlined_DPA_v2.pdf) and 2) a sample log export (log_schema_sample.csv). Both are stubs here — we will send official files from legal + infra as attachments in the contract packet.

Topline commitments for the pilot (confirming what we can sign up to):
- Roles: we will accept processor role limited to inference and transient outputs. Redwood will include explicit language that Customer Content will not be used to train or improve models without Customer's prior written consent.
- Residency: for the pilot we will lock hosting to our us-west region (US-only) and provide a written confirmation of the region-bound deployment for the pilot term.
- Logs & retention: we can offer a retention tier of 180 days for the pilot with an option to increase to 365 days. We support CSV export and syslog streaming for audit purposes.
- Notifications: we commit to an initial technical alert within 48 hours of detecting a relevant subprocessor incident and a formal written summary within 72 hours. For material data-impact incidents we will follow up with a full impact assessment within 7 calendar days.

Next steps:
1) Legal (Laura) will review and send a final redline within 2 business days.
2) Ops/infra (Priyom) will provision a us-west-locked tenant for the pilot and share the export sample endpoint details.
3) Let's book a 30-min ops call next Tuesday (Jul 9) to walk through the log format and residency proof. I'll propose times via calendar.

If those commitments look good, please reply to confirm and we'll queue the contract packet.

Thanks again —
Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com

--
Attachments included (sent via drive link in contract packet): redlined_DPA_v2.pdf, log_schema_sample.csv
